# Jubilees Chapter 22 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Abraham Blesses Jacob; Abraham's Death

---

**22:1** And it came-to-pass in the first year of the first week of the forty-third jubilee, that Abraham returned and dwelt opposite Hebron, which is Mamre.

**22:2** And Isaac slaughtered a peace-offering and brought it to his father Abraham, and Abraham ate. And Isaac's wife also brought gifts, and Ishmael's wife brought gifts. And they ate together. And Abraham rejoiced, for Isaac had slaughtered a peace-offering.

**22:3** And in those days Isaac also slaughtered a peace-offering to the LORD, and on the Feast of First-Fruits of the harvest he sent to his father Abraham some of the first-fruits of all the produce of the field and of the firstlings.

**22:4** And Abraham rejoiced greatly and blessed the Most High God who had created heaven and earth, and who had made all the fat-things of the earth and had given them to the sons of men that they might eat and drink and bless their Creator.

**22:5** "And now I give thanks to you, my God, because you have shown to me this day. Behold, I am one hundred and seventy-five years old, old and full of days, and all the days of my life have been peace unto me."

**22:6** "And I was separated from the nations, and from the impurity of the gentiles, and I dwelt among them; but I did not walk in the error of the nations, and I did not go after them and after their abominations."

**22:7** "And you, the living God, you know that the desires of my heart were to do your will, and to walk uprightly, and that I turned not to the right hand nor to the left in all my days."

**22:8** And Abraham called Jacob and said: "Come my son, come near, that I may kiss you, my beloved son."

**22:9** And Jacob came near and he kissed him, and he said: "My son, my beloved, there is nothing whatever in this world that rejoices my heart as much as you, and may the LORD bless you always, and may you be blessed above all the seed of men. Because you are the Lord and Light of the nations, you are the son of Abraham who was counted righteous before the LORD."

**22:10** "For in you and in your seed shall Abraham rejoice before me, and shall be named a prince and blessed before the LORD. Now I command you, my son, observe the commandments of Abraham your father. Keep his righteousness and his ways."

**22:11** "And associate not with the nations, and eat not with them, and do not according to their works, and do not become their companion, for their works are unclean, and all their ways are abomination and uncleanness."

**22:12** "They offer their sacrifices to the dead and they worship demons, and they eat over graves, and all their works are vanity and nothingness."

**22:13** "They have no heart to understand, and their eyes do not see what their works are, and how they err in saying to a piece of wood: 'You are my god,' and to a piece of stone: 'You are my lord, and you are my deliverer.' And these have no heart."

**22:14** "And you, my son Jacob, may God Most High help you and the God of heaven bless you. And may he remove you from their uncleanness and from all their error."

**22:15** "Be careful, my son Jacob, that you do not take a wife from any of the seed of the daughters of Canaan, for all his seed is to be rooted-out from the earth, because when Ham sinned, Canaan also sinned and his seed is destined for destruction upon the earth and for being rooted-out, and all who remain of him shall be scattered upon the earth."

**22:16** "For on account of the transgression of Ham, Noah cursed Canaan, and all his seed is rooted-out from the earth. Because of the uncleanness of his work he will go astray and be plucked up by the roots."

**22:17** "And now I give you, my son, all my commands; keep them. Do not marry from the daughters of Canaan, but take a wife for yourself from the seed of my family — a wife worthy of my son."

**22:18** "May the LORD God of Abraham bless you and bless your seed, and sanctify you as a holy nation, after the likeness of his own will, that you might keep his law and his righteousness. And may he be your Father and you his firstborn son and people for all time."

**22:19** "And do you go in peace, my son. May the Most High God, my God and your God, strengthen you to do his will and bless all your seed and the remnant of my seed, throughout the generations of the earth, forever, with the blessing with which he has blessed me."

**22:20** And Abraham concluded blessing Jacob, and then he lay upon his bed and was gathered to his fathers.

**22:21** And Jacob stood before his father Isaac after the death of his father Abraham. And Isaac loved Jacob.

**22:22** And in those days Isaac and Ishmael came from the well of the oath, and they dwelt with Abraham in the days of the feast. And Ishmael came with his four sons and with his six sons who were then alive, and they all came together.

**22:23** And Abraham's servants, and Isaac's servants, and Ishmael's servants came and buried Abraham — in the double-cave near Sarah his wife, in the field of Ephron the Hittite facing Mamre, the field which Abraham had bought from the sons of Heth.

**22:24** And they mourned for Abraham forty days, all the sons of his house, and Isaac and Ishmael and all their sons, and all the sons of Keturah in their places. And the weeping for Abraham was great.

---
*EMET notes: Feast of First-Fruits = Shavuot/Feast of Weeks, central to Jubilees' calendar. "Double-cave" = Cave of Machpelah. Abraham's deathbed blessing of Jacob (not Isaac blessing Jacob) is unique to Jubilees. "Root-out" applied to Canaan's seed is a recurring Jubilees judgment formula.*
